status: wave-4: pieces occupy lattice elements (volume, face, edge), not cell slots

shapes.design_purpose: The starting shape. Two units per block equals one harvest swing, so a small shelter visibly eats into a resource node instead of feeling free.

A thin partition standing on a vertical face of the lattice, centred on the plane the two neighbouring cells share, so it belongs to neither cell and a cube can fill either side of it. Snaps to the nearest vertical face to the crosshair - no rotation key. Half the cost of a cube so walling a shelter is cheaper than filling it.

Stands on a vertical edge of the lattice - the line where up to four walls meet - so it always lines up with the panels around it and stacks on the post below when you aim at its top. Corners where walls meet grow a post visual on their own; the placed post is for free-standing frames and for making a corner load-bearing in the player's eye.

Runs along a horizontal edge of the lattice, the line a wall's top and a floor's rim share, so it reads as a lintel over a doorway, a wall plate along the top of a wall, or a rail along a slab's edge depending only on what it is next to.

Half height and half depth, resting on the floor of its cell and turned with R (the one starting shape with a direction); the cheapest way to climb your own building. A proper stair piece is slice 2 of the building intensive.

The visible reward for the first Forge Tyrant kill (trial.json completion_unlock): a slab lying on a horizontal face of the lattice - the plane between a cell and the one above - that makes floors and roofs possible, so the trial demonstrably widens what can be built. Same thickness as a wall so a floor's rim and a wall's top meet cleanly.

design_purpose: grid_size_metres balances Minecraft-like constraint against detail (final value is an open question in construction.md). placement_range_metres is measured from the third-person camera, which sits about 4.5 m behind the player, so it must cover that set-back plus reach; 6 m could not reach the floor in front of the player. removal_refund_fraction controls experimentation freedom versus commitment and deliberately mirrors salvage_return_fraction in crafting.json so building and crafting feel like one economy. element (block | wall | floor | post | beam) says which kind of lattice element a shape occupies: a block takes a whole cell, a wall a vertical face shared by two cells, a floor a horizontal face, a post a vertical edge shared by four cells, a beam a horizontal edge. Placement snaps to the nearest free element of that kind to the crosshair, and two pieces only conflict when they want the same element - which is what lets a cube sit against a wall, a post stand where two walls meet, and a slab rim carry a beam, with no slot bookkeeping and no rotation key for anything but oriented blocks.
